record.paper_title: Some Open Questions about Symplectic 4-Manifolds, Singular Plane Curves, and Braid Group Factorizations
record.original_question: Let X_1 and X_2 be integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with the same values of c_1^2, c_2, c_1·[ω], and [ω]^2. Determine whether X_2 can always be obtained from X_1 by a finite sequence of Luttinger surgeries, where a Luttinger surgery cuts out a neighborhood of an embedded Lagrangian torus and reglues it by a twist along a chosen essential loop so that the resulting 4-manifold remains symplectic.

evidence.quote: Question 2.6. Let X1, X2 be two integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with the same (c_1^2, c_2, c_1 · [ω], [ω]^2). Is it always possible to obtain X2 from X1 by a sequence of Luttinger surgeries?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A symplectic 4-manifold is a smooth closed 4-manifold $X$ equipped with a closed non-degenerate 2-form $\omega$. Call such $(X,\omega)$ integral if the cohomology class $[\omega] \in H^2(X;\mathbb{R})$ lies in the image of $H^2(X;\mathbb{Z})$. Associated to $(X,\omega)$ are the Chern numbers $c_1^2[X]$ and $c_2[X]$ of the almost complex structure compatible with $\omega$, together with the symplectic invariants $c_1(X,\omega)\cdot[\omega]$ and $[\omega]^2$.

A Luttinger surgery on $(X,\omega)$ is the following operation: choose an embedded Lagrangian torus $T\subset X$ (whose tubular neighborhood is symplectomorphic to a neighborhood of the zero section in $T^*T^2$), choose an essential embedded loop $\gamma\subset T$, remove a tubular neighborhood of $T$, and reglue $T^2\times D^2$ by a diffeomorphism of the boundary 3-torus that performs a Dehn twist along $\gamma$ together with an integer number of meridional twists. The resulting 4-manifold carries a canonical symplectic structure extending $\omega$ outside the surgery region.

Question: Let $(X_1,\omega_1)$ and $(X_2,\omega_2)$ be two integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds satisfying
$$c_1^2[X_1]=c_1^2[X_2],\quad c_2[X_1]=c_2[X_2],\quad c_1\cdot[\omega_1]=c_1\cdot[\omega_2],\quad [\omega_1]^2=[\omega_2]^2.$$
Is it always possible to obtain $(X_2,\omega_2)$ from $(X_1,\omega_1)$ by a finite sequence of Luttinger surgeries?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a well-known open problem posed as a conjectural picture for symplectic 4-manifolds. Subsequent work has used Luttinger surgery to construct many exotic small symplectic 4-manifolds and to relate symplectic manifolds with the same Chern numbers, but no general affirmative or negative answer to the surgery-equivalence question has been established. Recent papers (e.g., on unchaining surgery and exotic 4-manifolds via Luttinger surgery on Lefschetz fibrations) continue to investigate the question without resolving it.

status_evidence.snippet: Question 2.6 asks whether two integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with the same (c_1^2, c_2, c_1·[ω], [ω]^2) can always be related by a sequence of Luttinger surgeries.
status_evidence.claim: Original formulation as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Unchaining surgery and topology of symplectic 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study how surgery operations such as Luttinger surgery relate symplectic 4-manifolds with prescribed invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Question continues to motivate ongoing research without a known resolution.

status_evidence.title: Constructions of small symplectic 4-manifolds using Luttinger surgery
status_evidence.snippet: Luttinger surgery is used to produce many exotic symplectic 4-manifolds, illustrating the breadth of the surgery operation.
status_evidence.claim: Provides supporting evidence for the conjectural picture but no general theorem.
